cultural.vision_reason: This is a jillāyeh, a woman's reversible coat with cross-stitch embroidery and appliqué patches, a garment style associated with Central Asian Jewish and Tajik/Bukharan communities; it is consistent with traditional Tajik dress.

physical.title: coat (jillāyeh)
physical.summary: Woman's reversible coat with elbow-length sleeves, known as jillāyeh, made of  indigo-dyed cotton with taffeta (heremzi) appliqué patches in red, yellow and  green as well as ikat and 'atlas' satin appliqué patches along the front and on the sleeves. The back is richly embroidered on the inside mostly in cross-stitch with  multicoloured silks.  The coat is reversible and could be worn inside- out, the inner lapels embroidered in cross-stitch in red and white.    The coat has a yoke and under-arm inserts of blue cotton.

cultural.vision_reason: A woman's coat combining indigo cotton, ikat/atlas silk panels, and cross-stitch embroidery — materials and techniques consistent with Central Asian (Tajik/Uzbek) village dress; garment type fits the claimed ethnicity's traditional attire.

physical.title: coat (jillāyeh)
physical.summary: Village woman's short-sleeved coat (jillāyeh), made of indigo-dyed cotton with satin (ikat and atlas), taffeta and cotton appliqué patches along the front in various shades of red, yellow and green.  The coat also has panels of multi-coloured embroidery in a variety of stitches, including open-work and cross-stitch, along the sleeves as well as on the side and back skirt panels. The coat could be reversed and worn inside-out, the inner lapels embroidered in cross-stitch in shades of yellow, green, white, blue, black and red.  The coat has a yoke and under-arm inserts of red cotton and is trimmed along the neck-line with red satin and along the front opening with red cotton cord.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a Palestinian village woman's dress (thob jinneh u nar) with cross-stitch embroidery, Syrian silk panels, and pointed sleeves — a classic Levantine/Palestinian garment style, not Tajik dress from Central Asia; the metadata itself describes Syrian textiles and Arabic garment terminology.

physical.title: dress (thob jinneh u nar)
physical.summary: Village woman's dress (thob) with large pointed sleeves (irdan) made of white coloured cotton with red and green silk stripes at the selvage (jinneh u nar) and strips of different types of coloured textile stitched together in squares or rectangles. These include striped (atlas), patterned (othmani) and ikat (lisan il asfur) Syrian silk satins, velvets and impiorted cottons. The side panels are made of red and green Syrian silk taffeta (heremzi), embroidered with cross-stich in bright colours. The chest panel (qabbeh), standing collar and hem are embroidered with fishbone stitch, close herringbone stitch and cross-stitch in a variety of bright colours. The dress is stitched together using a loose herringbone stitch and loose zigzag connecting stitch (manjal halall.)

physical.title: dress (thob)
physical.summary: Village woman’s dress (thob) made of indigo dyed cotton. The standing collar is embroidered with cross stitch embroidery in floss silk and  the yoke (radha) is made of red and yellow ikat Syrian silk satin (lisan-il-asfur).The long pointed sleeves (irdan) are made of indigo dyed cotton with deep magenta, green and cream selvedge stripes. The top sleeves (sawa’id) are made of red and orange silk taffeta (heremzi) embroidered with cross-stitch, joined together with joining stitch (manajel) and finished with interlaced cross-stitch in vividly coloured silk floss. The chest panel (qabbeh), side panels (banayeq) and back of skirt panel (shinyar) are embroidered are embroidered with cross-stitching mainly red and embellished differently coloured floss silk. The front of the skirt is appliqued with floss silk embroidered burgundy and peach silk taffeta panels. The rim of the skirt is also appliqued with a band of cross-stitch embroidered silk taffeta. The hem is reinforced with fishbone stitch embroidery in differently coloured cotton and silk thread.
